slides.texte_overlay:
5 hobbies that will pull you out
of your dopamine addiction

pottery

take a pottery class and feel how slow it is to shape one bowl. clay can't be rushed, and an hour of it quiets a brain that's used to a new thing every second.

long distance cycling

ride for an hour with no music, just the road and your breath. long, steady effort teaches your brain that good feelings can come from patience, not just speed.

growing herbs

grow basil or mint on your windowsill and look after it every morning. waiting days to see a new leaf is the perfect, gentle antidote to a world of instant everything.

learning instead of scrolling

every time you open a feed, close it and learn one real thing instead: a planet, a painting, a moment in history. real rewards slowly replace the empty ones.

jigsaw evenings

keep a big puzzle on a table and add pieces in the evening instead of watching shorts. slow, quiet focus is exactly what an overstimulated mind needs to recover.
